claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Pack cementation can deposit a thin, uniform aluminide coating on HfNbTaTiZr.
An aluminide coating on HfNbTaTiZr will form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface layer at high temperature.
The Al2O3 layer will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion with the Al2O3 layer will reduce oxidation of HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminide coating and associated oxidation exposure will not alter the bulk microstructure responsible for the alloy's mechanical performance.
Aluminide-coated HfNbTaTiZr will show lower oxidation-induced weight gain than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure in air at 1000 °C for up to 100 hours.
Aluminide-coated HfNbTaTiZr will develop a thinner oxide scale than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure in air at 1000 °C for up to 100 hours.
Aluminide-coated HfNbTaTiZr will retain the room-temperature tensile ductility of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after high-temperature exposure.
Aluminide-coated HfNbTaTiZr will retain the high-temperature yield strength of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes significant oxidation and compromised performance during high-temperature exposure in air.
The coating's protective benefit is expected to persist around 1000 °C for exposures up to 100 hours.
The proposed protection and mechanical-property retention apply under tensile or creep loading associated with strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
